confidence_notes: I used two web searches. The first found the RBA observation of 0.6720 USD per AUD for 2026-11-18. That figure was reported in the search summary. I did not read it directly on the RBA's official table page. The second search found crowd-sourced cost-of-living figures from mylifeelsewhere.com: a basic meal at about USD 2.9–3.1, a pint of domestic beer at about USD 2.0–2.2 (range 1.5–3.5) and a cappuccino at about USD 1.7–2.1. I set the restaurant draft beer anchor a little above the crowd-sourced average because I expect tourist-area venues to charge more. I raised the cappuccino figure slightly for café prices. The mid-range meal is my own estimate, about 1,000 THB for two. I did not search for cocktail or wine prices. Cocktails are based on local prices running about 2.5–3 times beer. Wine is based on imported wine being heavily taxed in Thailand, so a glass costs about 180–220 THB. The accommodation figures are my own estimates from general knowledge for July, which is low-to-shoulder season in Hua Hin. I did not check any booking sites. Hua Hin has few registered hostels, so the dorm and private-room anchors are less certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Hua Hin is a Thai beach resort that attracts domestic visitors, expats and retirees. Its prices are similar to Pattaya and somewhat lower than Phuket's main beach areas. Food is cheap in local restaurants, while imported wine and cocktails cost more.
